text.name: TextDesc2
text.text: Uzebox is an open-source DIY video game console created to demonstrate that simple microcontrollers can be used for gaming. Released in 2008, it uses an AVR microcontroller and custom software to generate graphics, sound, and controller input without a dedicated graphics processor. The platform supports homebrew games, emulators, and community-developed software while encouraging users to build and program their own console hardware. Uzebox is known for its open design and educational approach to game development.
